YOUR ROOFING QUESTIONS

A clearer way forward.

Practical information for the decisions ahead.

How much will it cost to repair or replace my roof?

The existing website lists general ranges of $7,000–$35,000 for a full replacement and $300–$1,500 for minor repairs. These are published guidance, not a current quote. Roof size, material, access, concealed damage, and the scope affect pricing. Request a written estimate for your property.

How long will the repair or replacement process take?

The existing site gives general guidance of 1–2 days for repairs and 1–3 days for replacement. Weather, inspections, delivery, concealed damage, size, and complexity can change the schedule. Confirm the expected timeline for your project.

What type of roofing materials should I choose?

Compare shingles, metal, tile, and membrane systems against roof slope, structural requirements, site exposure, maintenance, appearance, and budget. Ask for a product-specific recommendation rather than choosing by material name alone.

Are you licensed and insured?

Near Shore Roofing’s current website states that the company is licensed and insured. Ask the team for current documentation before authorizing work.

Will the work be covered by warranty?

The company mentions warranties but does not publish complete terms. Ask which workmanship and manufacturer warranties apply to your proposed work, including exclusions, transfer provisions, and maintenance requirements.

Do you offer financing?

The existing website advertises financing. Contact the company for current availability, the application process, eligibility, and written terms. No rates or approval guarantees are published here.

Can a leaking roof be repaired without replacing it?

Sometimes. A localized flashing or material defect may be repairable when the surrounding assembly remains sound. Widespread wear, repeated leaks, or deterioration beneath the surface may make replacement more practical. An inspection should establish the scope.

What should I do about a ceiling water stain?

Record when it appears and whether it changes during rain. Move belongings away if safe and arrange an assessment. Plumbing or condensation can also cause stains, so the source must be checked. Keep clear of sagging ceilings and electrical hazards.

How often should a roof be inspected?

Set an inspection schedule around the roof’s age, condition, manufacturer guidance, and exposure. Arrange an assessment after suspected damage or a new leak. Observe from the ground rather than climbing onto the roof yourself.

How long will a shingle roof last in Florida?

There is no single dependable number for every roof. Product, installation, ventilation, exposure, maintenance, and storm history affect service life. Evaluate the roof’s condition instead of relying on age alone.

How should I prepare my roof for hurricane season?

Arrange maintenance early, keep drainage paths clear using suitable professional help, and address known loose or damaged roofing. Document the roof’s condition. Follow local emergency instructions whenever a storm threatens; maintenance is not a guarantee against damage.

How does salt air affect roofing choices?

Coastal exposure can influence corrosion risk and product warranty limitations. Ask about material, coating, fastener compatibility, distance-from-water restrictions, and maintenance instructions for the exact proposed system.

What should I ask before hiring a roofing contractor?

Request current licensing and insurance documentation, a written scope, product details, payment schedule, cleanup plan, permit responsibilities, change-order process, and written warranty terms. Compare complete scopes.

What happens during a roof replacement?

A typical project includes site preparation, removal as specified, assessment of the deck, approved repairs, protective layers, installation, flashing and edge details, cleanup, and required inspections. Confirm the sequence and scope for your specific roof.
